body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\), the set of all \((s,h)\) induced by full-data laws \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\) that agree with \(P\) is exactly \(\mathcal K(P)\). In particular, all layerwise stayer and harm coordinates satisfying the displayed hinge inequalities are jointly attainable by one normalized full-data law.
body.justification: Coordinatewise bounds are insufficient for an aggregate ratio unless a single law attains every chosen coordinate simultaneously.
body.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds. De Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp multi-tier benefit and harm bounds when the tiers are categories of the outcome itself. Possebom--Riva and Kallus characterize binary harm couplings. None of these results allocates selectively observed units across latent same-layer stayers or gives the exact cross-world stayer--harm prism for protocol-assigned selection tiers.
body.consumer: A protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiment can report harm among participants whose assigned tier would be unchanged under either assignment.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\).  We first prove necessity.  For any agreeing \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\), let
\[
p_{ij}=P^{\star}(D_0=i,D_1=j).
\]
Random assignment identifies its row and column margins with \(r\) and \(c\), and strong tier monotonicity makes it upper triangular.  The diagonal-box theorem therefore yields
\[
\ell_d\le s_d=p_{dd}\le u_d.
\]
The event counted by \(h_d\) is contained in each of the events defining \(s_d\), \(q_{0d}\), and the treatment-arm failure mass \(c_d-q_{1d}\).  Hence
\[
h_d\le\min\{s_d,q_{0d},c_d-q_{1d}\}=\min\{s_d,b_d\}.
\]
Among the \(q_{0d}\) mass with \(D_0=d\) and \(Y_{0,d}=1\), at most \(r_d-s_d\) are upgraded, exactly \(h_d\) are harmed stayers, and the remaining successful stayers have \(Y_{1,d}=1\) and hence have mass at most \(q_{1d}\).  Therefore
\[
q_{0d}\le (r_d-s_d)+h_d+q_{1d},
\]
or
\[
h_d\ge s_d-r_d+q_{0d}-q_{1d}=s_d-a_d.
\]
Together with \(h_d\ge0\), these are exactly the inequalities defining \(\mathcal K(P)\).

For sufficiency, take an arbitrary \((s,h)\in\mathcal K(P)\).  By the diagonal-box theorem, choose an upper-triangular layer coupling \(p\in\Theta(P)\) with \(p_{dd}=s_d\).  For each positive layer define
\[
x_d=\max\{h_d,q_{0d}-(r_d-s_d)\},
\qquad
y_d=\max\{x_d-h_d,q_{1d}-(c_d-s_d)\}.
\]
The prism inequalities and the observable cell inequalities give
\[
h_d\le x_d\le\min\{q_{0d},s_d\},
\qquad
x_d-h_d\le q_{1d}.
\]
Indeed, the only non-immediate inequality is the last one, and it follows from
\[
h_d\ge s_d-a_d=s_d-r_d+q_{0d}-q_{1d}.
\]
Likewise,
\[
x_d-h_d\le y_d\le\min\{q_{1d},s_d-h_d\}.
\]
For its second upper bound, the term \(q_{1d}-(c_d-s_d)\) is at most \(s_d-h_d\) because \(h_d\le c_d-q_{1d}\); all other inequalities follow from \(s_d\le c_d\), \(x_d\le s_d\), and nonnegativity.

Split the diagonal mass \(p_{dd}=s_d\) into the four outcome cells
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&Y_{1,d}=0&Y_{1,d}=1\\ \hline
Y_{0,d}=0&s_d-y_d-h_d&y_d-x_d+h_d\\
Y_{0,d}=1&h_d&x_d-h_d
\end{array}.
\]
All four entries are nonnegative by the preceding inequalities.  Their sum is \(s_d\), their control-success margin is \(x_d\), their treatment-success margin is \(y_d\), and their harm entry is \(h_d\).

It remains to label the off-diagonal layer mass.  For each positive left layer \(i\), the required residual control-success mass is \(q_{0i}-x_i\), and
\[
0\le q_{0i}-x_i\le r_i-s_i=\sum_{j>i}p_{ij}.
\]
Distribute this amount arbitrarily among the capacities \((p_{ij}:j>i)\).  For each positive right layer \(j\), independently distribute the residual treatment-success mass \(q_{1j}-y_j\) among the incoming capacities \((p_{ij}:i<j)\); this is possible because
\[
0\le q_{1j}-y_j\le c_j-s_j=\sum_{i<j}p_{ij}.
\]
On an off-diagonal arc of mass \(p_{ij}\) with \(i>0\), let \(A_{ij}\in[0,p_{ij}]\) and \(B_{ij}\in[0,p_{ij}]\) be its allocated left- and right-success masses.  Choose
\[
t_{ij}^{11}\in
\left[\max\{0,A_{ij}+B_{ij}-p_{ij}\},\min\{A_{ij},B_{ij}\}\right]
\]
and set
\[
t_{ij}^{10}=A_{ij}-t_{ij}^{11},\quad
t_{ij}^{01}=B_{ij}-t_{ij}^{11},\quad
t_{ij}^{00}=p_{ij}-A_{ij}-B_{ij}+t_{ij}^{11}.
\]
The displayed interval is nonempty because \(A_{ij},B_{ij}\le p_{ij}\), so these four masses are nonnegative and have the required two binary margins.  For an arc from \(0^{\star}\), only the right-success label is required, and it is split directly according to its allocated right-success mass.  The arc \(0^{\star}\to0^{\star}\) requires no outcome label.

The resulting expanded-state coupling has margins \(\mu_0,\mu_1\), is supported on admissible arcs, and has precisely the prescribed \((s,h)\).  The expanded-network decoder lifts it to one normalized full-data law in \(\mathcal M_L\) agreeing with \(P\).  Every coordinate was chosen before this single completion, so attainability is joint, including on faces created by zero cells.  Necessity and sufficiency prove that the identified joint region is exactly \(\mathcal K(P)\).
